findings.passage: In April 2023, when DC's James Gunn publicly backed her show, she would not treat the good news as settled. A Three tends to bank a positive signal from an authority and move on; withholding belief until an outcome is "a definitive" is a security reflex.
findings.problem: The article's main pre-promotional discriminator against Type 3 is an ordinary, correct piece of industry realism, framed with an unsourced type generalization. In the same Just Jared Jr. answer she says Gunn's tweet had moved things to "a little bit of 50-50", so she did partly bank the signal. Her caution also proved accurate: two months later her regular role was cut. The remark is used in four places (Superman & Lois section, "Borrowed certainty", the Type 3 case, FAQ 3) as if it discriminates more than it does.
findings.acceptance_test: Where the Gunn remark carries the Six-vs-Three argument, the prose notes that the caution was ordinary and proved warranted (or quotes the "50-50" line) and says it leans rather than separates. "A Three tends to bank a positive signal..." is either sourced or softened to a labeled reading. The Six-vs-Three conclusion stays "live second alternative", and FAQ 3 matches.

findings.passage: When an interviewer's question turned on Barker's memory of how a sequence came together, she deferred to it: "if that's what Curry said, then that's definitely what happened."
findings.problem: The quote leaves out her stated reason. In S11 09:21-09:31 it directly follows "because we shot this two years ago, there's some things that I kind of go". Deferring to a director's memory of a shoot you half-remember is ordinary, so as borrowed-certainty evidence the line reads stronger than its context supports.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence either includes or accurately reflects the memory reason (for example, "saying they shot it two years ago, she deferred to it"), or the line is no longer counted as evidence of borrowed certainty. C23's inference records the context.

findings.passage: For a Six, trust works like infrastructure: once it is in place, the risky work can begin.
findings.problem: At 4,373 words the article runs well past the standard's roughly 2,000-3,500 target, and much of the excess is repetition rather than new portrait. The central pattern is restated in the hook, the type answer, "What she describes is the Six sequence", and this infrastructure metaphor. The Gunn remark appears four times. The Type 7, Type 3 and other-rivals sections stack hedge on hedge ("It counts for less than it seems, though...", "though not by a knockout"), which slows the second half.
findings.acceptance_test: Each recurring point (the name-secure-move pattern, the Gunn remark) is argued in full once and only briefly referenced elsewhere. Hedge chains in the rival sections are consolidated so each concession is made once. Every verified detail and every protected passage survives, the type answer stays at 60 words or fewer, and the article moves meaningfully toward the standard's word target without new claims.
